summary:
Space Mission Design Game is an interactive 2D educational aerospace simulation built in Unity that teaches students and aspiring engineers how NASA designs CubeSat missions using the real Concept Maturity Level (CML 1–4) engineering lifecycle.

Players select from three NASA-inspired missions—BioNutrients-2 (ISS 400 km), BisonSat (600 km Polar Sun-Synchronous Orbit), and Artemis Lunar Ice Pathfinder (384,400 km Lunar Orbit)—and engineer a 1U, 3U, or 6U CubeSat within strict mass, power, budget, and telemetry constraints. Before launch, players face real NASA CubeSat 101 engineering trade-off dilemmas (such as burn-wire redundancy and NOAA licensing) at a CML 4 review gate. Approved missions launch via a multi-stage 2D Starship sequence (including LEO orbital refueling, Trans-Lunar Injection, and Lunar Orbit Insertion for Artemis) into a live 2D orbital simulation with 1x–128x time warp, realistic sunlit Earth/night-side shading, and a post-mission NASA CML Scorecard.
details:
How It Works:

  1. CML 1 — Mission Selection: Choose between 3 progressive NASA CubeSat missions (Easy: ISS Microgravity Lab, Medium: Polar Earth Forest Imager, Hard: Artemis Lunar Ice Pathfinder).
  2. CML 2–3 — Spacecraft Builder: Assemble bus frame, launch vehicle, target orbit, science payload, solar array, battery, ADCS, radio, and ground station while balancing real-time Mass, Power, Budget, Data Rate, and Science Score margins.
  3. CML 4 — Pre-Launch Review Gate: Resolve CubeSat 101 engineering dilemmas (burn-wire redundancy, NOAA imaging licensing, JPL 35% mass/power margins) that directly affect flight performance and Chief Engineer debrief logs.
  4. Phase C/D — Launch & 2D Orbit Simulation: Watch a mission-specific 2D Starship launch sequence (ISS 400 km, Polar SSO 600 km circularization, or Artemis Lunar LEO Tanker Refueling + TLI + Moon approach + LOI), then monitor your CubeSat in 2D orbit with 1x–128x time warp, sunlight/night-side terminator shading, and real orbital period tracking.
  5. Post-Mission Scorecard: Review mission success, resource margins, and NASA Chief Engineer feedback.

Tools & Tech Stack:

  • Engine & Language: Unity 6 (2D URP), C#, TextMeshPro
  • Procedural Graphics & Audio: Custom procedural 2D vector sprites (Texture2D) and synthesized AudioClip sound effects (Raptor engine rumble, stage separation, UI/telemetry cues) with zero external copyrighted assets.
dataRefs: NASA CubeSat 101: Basic Concepts and Processes for First-Time CubeSat Developers
